I’m a 4th-year Ph.D. candidate in Computer Science & Biochemistry and Molecular Genetics at Northwestern University, co-advised by Prof. Han Liu and Prof. Yaping Liu. My research focuses on recursively self-improving AI agents for scientific discovery, advancing noninvasive early cancer detection using cell-free DNA and personalized cancer treatment through DNA/RNA vaccine design.

Previously, I received my bachelor’s degree in Mathematics from Fudan University in 2023, advised by Prof. Tao Chen, and was recognized as an Outstanding Graduate of Fudan University.

I share research stories, experiments, and ideas on my Blog.

Research directions

My work spans four interconnected areas: genomic foundation models, model infrastructure, sequence design, and recursively self-improving scientific agents.

Genomic foundation models

Including GenomeOcean for genomic sequence understanding and design.

GenomeOceanDNABERT-S

Model infrastructure

Including Genome-Factory for genomic model deployment and adaptation.

Genome-Factory

Sequence design

Including D-DOIT for DNA/RNA design toward personalized cancer vaccines, alongside DiMOS and DoMinO for sequence design.

D-DOITDiMOSDoMinO

Recursively self-improving scientific agents

Including SciMARS, toward integrating models, tools, and feedback for iterative scientific discovery.

Entrepreneurship

Quantitative Investment Association

I’m interested in entrepreneurship in AI for scientific discovery and medical science. During my undergraduate studies, I founded the Quantitative Investment Association (QIA), the largest nonprofit organization in quantitative finance in China, connecting students, researchers, and industry professionals in quantitative finance.

Research intern recruitment

I host research interns working on genomic foundation models, scientific sequence design, and AI agents for medical science, with GPU resources available for experiments. If you’re interested, email me your CV and a short summary of your research experience.
